utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, everybody. Before we have the next witness, are there any matters that the parties would like to raise at this stage? Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours. Just a small matter that I think we may need some clarification for the record for purposes. Yesterday, Ms. Issa quoted from the Borovcanin transcript that was -- he gave two statements. One was on February 20th 2002 and one was in 11 March 2002. We don't know which one. But the question that was posed after the exchange that we had with respect to whether it should be used or not used was this, and I'm quoting. I have the unofficial transcript, but it's from page 57, line 25, and it goes on. It says: "Sir, Mr. Borovcanin told the office of the Prosecutor investigators that Milos Stupar was there, and that he found you and Mr. Stupar and asked you not to move from that position." From reading, this it would appear he found both of them together at the same time. Of course, the witness indicated he had not seen Mr. Stupar. So I would like to know, because I went through the transcript of the two statements, clearly Mr. Borovcanin says that he saw Mr. Stupar there, and that he saw Mr. -- the other witness there. But I don't see anywhere in the transcript where it says or at least where it's clear that you can draw some inference that they were together at the time when he saw them. And so I would some clarification. Perhaps Mr. McCloskey can ask Ms. Issa where it was in the record so that this can be clarified. Because if that's not the case, then I just don't want the Court to give -- to have the impression that the witness was less than candid when he said he didn't see Mr. Stupar as a result of what Mr. Borovcanin said. Am I being clear, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think you are quite clear, and I quite understand what you are saying. And during the cross-examination, I believe that the hearsay evidence could be used as a base for the cross-examination. And as for what kind of conclusion the Trial Chamber will arrive is another matter. And we'll put the last testimony of the witness at the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, I didn't intervene yesterday as I would normally intervene because I thought the Court was getting a little bit perhaps irritated, to use what I believe I felt at the time, because perhaps the Court thought I was intervening too much. I don't want there to be a misunderstanding as far as what Mr. Borovcanin said. The practice normally is for the attorney to read, this is what Mr. Borovcanin said so we have exactly what he said. Nothing in the statement indicates that he saw them both together. The question the way it was posed would give the impression that they were both together at the same time when Mr. Borovcanin saw them. All I want is to know where in the transcript that's there, because there's a -- she made a representation that is in the transcript. If it's not in the transcript, then at least we need to have some explanation why the question was posed in that fashion? Or at least the record to be clear that he saw both of them but not together at the same time. That's all I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I quite understand what you are saying. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we can clear it up. March 11th, 2002, page 40 in the English transcript. "Where did you actually travel do? Where did you meet up with your unit commanders?"

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: "I reached Sandici." Question: "And who did you meet there?"

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVCANIN
utterances.text: "I found Pantic and Stupar, and I forgot to tell you that Zoju Daniolo [phoen] was with me. Zoju Daniolo, he was with me."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It doesn't say they were together. He found both of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would appreciate if Mr. McCloskey would behave himself and conduct himself like a professional and not like a clown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I'm not happy with your language and the term you used in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm trying to make a point. I'm trying to make a record. And from the other side, we have, you know, these commotions. I'm not used to being in a courtroom where on the other side a professional conducts himself in that fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that Mr. McCloskey just tried to help you in this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I thought that the question put by Ms. Issa yesterday has no problem at all because I believe that the Prosecution also want to know, to make clear, whether they are together or not. So she posed this question. It will help us to understand the situation. And by the way, we'll have, you know, other witnesses to testify to this effect. If we could make this matter clear, it's better. It's for the benefit of all the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President. That's all I was trying to do, is to try to make it clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And another matter, yesterday we received bundles of the documents which are the statements furnished by the Defence counsel. Well, for this case, we have enough documents on our shelves, and I believe that in the future the Chamber only needs two sets of the documents consisting of the previous statements of the witness. No more than that. I believe that will reduce the burdens from the Defence team, to copy so many documents. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's fine. I was unaware that we had been making these copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's piled up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I'm sure it was done. I just was unaware of it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you ready for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There are none, Your Honour. He was questioned as a suspect. I will go into it in great detail as to that matter. And he had indicated that he understood. He's a police officer. He understood the nature of it at the time. He understands the ramifications today. And he wishes to testify in open, public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I doubt very much about the phrase "go into it in great detail." You could mention that but do not go into the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In this instance, Your Honour, again, I don't mean to be disputatious or argumentative; however, there is a portion that I want to bring out to the Court's attention. There are a couple of pages where the gentleman gave a description of the events. Mr. McCloskey entered into the courtroom, and there was this huge exchange where Mr. McCloskey made some allegations against the gentleman. And then in spite of that, despite of being told that he was being untruthful and what have you, the gentleman again after being advised of his rights went ahead and gave some 80-plus pages of a statement. And I think it goes -- if we're going to judge somebody's credibility, I think that has to be taken into consideration. And I also want to make a very clear record as to how this man was questioned because I think in the manner in which he was questioned initially and advised of his lack of candor should be taken into consideration as a factor whether he should be believed or not believed versus other statements that the Prosecution is relying on, primarily Mr. Borovcanin who is no where to be found, you know, although he's wanted. And so, I think this is, this is necessary. But I'll try to be as brief as I possibly can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think the Chamber knows, we're not relying on the statements of Mr. Borovcanin. We sometimes use that in our questions to try to get at things. The interview with this man was perfectly appropriate and proper. If the Court would like to have a copy of that interview, I have no objection to that. But going into, you know, reading question by question by question and spending forever putting the Prosecution on trial is really not relevant and not appropriate. I have no problem with the interview as it was. And if Mr. Karnavas wants the Court to see it, fine. But this -- these attempts to paint the Prosecution in this manner is really -- at this point I would hope it would stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm entitled -- this is an open Court. It's open to the public. The public is entitled to know how the Prosecution is conducting their cases and how they are investigating their cases and how they are indicting people and bringing them to trial. In this instance, this man came as a suspect, was advised, and then was told that he was a liar and that he was lying and being untruthful. And this was over two or three pages of Mr. McCloskey basically telling him that he was a totally uncooperative liar and then gave him another opportunity to come clean. He was then advised of his rights. After that, the gentleman refused to have a lawyer and went ahead and gave from page 19 all the way to page 105 of a statement. I think this is necessary for the Court to consider. I think it's also necessary for the public to hear because this is after all a public trial. And might I add, two days ago, the Prosecutor stood up and said we have an executioner on the stand. That was front pages in the newspaper the following day. So if the Prosecutor can take those measures to demonstrate to the public who we have on trial and who we have as witnesses, I think I'm entitled to do the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey -- I'm sorry. Mr. Karnavas, I hope you could understand that here the subject matter is to see whether your client is innocent or not, but not other matters. I hope your questions will concentrate on this very issue. You could try how far you could go, but just be careful that -- do not put the other side on the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I normally don't do that. But we have this joint criminal enterprise. So it's not a matter of just focussing on the client. I have to attack everything else, including these crime-based witness statements that are -- crime-based evidence that has come in. Had he been charged as an aider and abettor or as a coperpetrator, it's different. But once you put him into this, Kafkaesque you know, form of criminal liability, you know, this beast called the joint criminal enterprise, something that is foreign to most of the world, then I'm compelled to at least attack each and every sector of it because otherwise if it goes unchallenged, then it comes into the judgement as something that's proven fact. And everything is connected. So I try to try the case that is relevant to Mr. Blagojevic but also, because a lot of things are interconnected, I have to attack them. And as you see, I'm trying to be as efficient as I possibly can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm not going to discuss with you at this moment about the concept of the joint criminal enterprise because it's a very difficult question. We have spent quite an amount of time on these procedural issues and actually while eating your time. So could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Would you please speak louder.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Will you please take the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you're going to need to speak up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us what your name is.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: My name is Milos Stupar, and I am from Sekovici, Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: S-t-u-p-a-r.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Stupar, you know that as you are testifying here today, you are still -- you still have the status of a suspect?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you were questioned by the Prosecutor on June 26th, 2002, and at that time you were questioned as a suspect, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, currently, you are a police officer, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What is your -- what do you currently -- where do you currently work?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I work at the police station at Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What is your position there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I'm an inspector for general crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long have you been a police officer?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: About 11 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Having worked for 11 years as a police officer and as an inspector of general crime, I take it you understand what it is to be a suspect?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you were questioned by the Prosecutor, you were advised, were you not, that you had certain rights, one of them being that you could have a lawyer there and you could choose not to even speak to them?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you speak to them?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: You mean to the lawyer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, no, to the Prosecutor, when they questioned you, after they advised you of your rights.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you have a lawyer there with you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, yesterday I provided you with a copy that we finally got that was a cleaned-up copy of your interview that was taken on 26 June 2002. Did you have a chance to read the cleaned-up version?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And before that, did you have an opportunity to read the previous version?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it that had been provided to you by the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it says here that they were going to provide you one within about -- shortly after the interview. When was it that you got a copy of your interview, statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I got that five or six days ago through some connections, not from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in reading your interview, it appears that initially you gave a general description of the events surrounding the fall of Srebrenica after -- primarily after June -- July 13, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And after that general description in your statement, it would appear, that a gentleman sitting over here, Mr. McCloskey, came into the room and then said that what you had been saying was untruthful lies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That's a misstatement of the question --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- and what I've said. And it's leading. And now of course he's going to want to read the whole thing, which is fine. Go ahead. But again, it's -- this is getting really sickening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please read that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could get it on the ELMO, and I have -- I'll be reading from page 14 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Page 14, and I can start at line 9. And there's a Srpski version that we have for you so you can follow along. All right. Now, sir, I'm reading from page 14, line 9 from the interview taken on 26 June 2002. "Now, we will be evaluating your statement, and we -- as we review you potential involvement in this case. So it's absolutely important that you tell us the truth and we, I can tell you, we have been investigating this case for over six years now. And many things have been clearly established. One thing, both from documents and from witness testimony, is that you were in command of a unit from Sekovici special police and from the beginning of this the police involvement in the operation through the last few days. I tell you this -- I tell you this because my colleague is telling me that you are telling them a story that you have just happened to be in places and that you were not command during the critical times. We view that as an untruth, as a lie. And as such, would be an obstruction of what we are trying to do here in getting to the truth. So before we even get into the details of this event, you are in more trouble than you need to be. You know that the army ran this operation, and we know the army made the decisions to murder people, and we know that MUP were under the command of the army and got sucked into this thing, is what it appears to us. So it's only with reluctance that we look at MUP commanders, and we are really -- are asking of the MUP is to tell us the truth because the truth will get down to the people that are most responsible, and that's who we are trying to get." And it goes on and on. And for the sake of time, I won't read the next three pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If I'm going to be on trial here, Your Honour, I think at least the Court should have the full part of it. We don't need to read it all, but it's a perfectly appropriate interview. As the witness said, he had no complaints at the end of the interview. So I would prefer that if this is going to be allowed, that you at least be provided with the document so you can see how it was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I could read the rest of it, too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there's no necessity because I believe that we have the interview already and we could read it by yourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. And I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you want, as an exception, you can offer to tender that interview into the evidence, as an exception. As an exception.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right, I understand, Your Honour. I understand. Just for the record, I would have read all the way through page 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But now, sir, at some point after this statement made to you made by Mr. McCloskey, were you not again advised of your rights?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me show you, if you could go on to the last page, page 18, it says here, you're told "and you understand your rights also as a suspect, and so you can stand on those rights at any time you wish." This is what Mr. McCloskey tells you. And I read from -- that would be on page 17 in the Srpski version around line 17. And in the English, it is page 18, line 2. So you're advised again that --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- you have rights. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then you're asked if you have any questions, and then the interview continues. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, before we talk about the events that are critical to this case, perhaps you could give us a little bit of background information. Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I was born in Sekovici, Municipality of Sekovici, on the 7th of December 1963. And that is where I reside. That is where I live at present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where did you go to school?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I went to school, primary school, in Tisca, and secondary school in Vlasenica. And I studied in Novi Sad. I went to university there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before becoming a police officer in I think you said it was 1993, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I worked in the firm in bauxite, and also I was a private caterer just before the outbreak of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that currently you are still a police officer, an inspector. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Have you been evaluated and certified recently by the IPTF, when they were going through the evaluations and certifications of the entire police force in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And they did give me a certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And aside from giving the statement to the Prosecution, have you been questioned by anyone else regarding these events, any commissions?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. I was questioned by a commission of the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And how many times have you appeared before the commission?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Four or five times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to focus your attention to July 1995. All right? Could you please tell us where you were working at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: In early July, I was on annual leave. I had left my former duty and was about to take up my new duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what was your former duty?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: As commander of the 2nd detachment of the Sekovici special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Briefly, if you could describe to us what this detachment was all about. Who did it belong to? Who was it supervised by? How it came into existence?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It was led by the commander of the special police brigade, Goran Saric. His deputy was Ljubisa Borovcanin. It consisted of six or seven detachments, the special brigade that is, and the 2nd Sekovici Detachment was one of these. Until the 15th of June 1995, I was the commander, and then I went on annual leave waiting for the document appointing me to my new duty --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, if I could stop you here because I want to take you step by step. Before we get there, to you taking leave, could you please tell us the size of this detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It always had between 80 and a hundred men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what sort of equipment was available to these men?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Mostly they had rifles. Most of them had flak jackets, not all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did they have any tanks, Pragas, any other hardware?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, there was a support platoon which had a tank, a Praga, and 68 and 82-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was that part of the 2nd detachment, or was that part of another unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It was part of the 2nd detachment, and it was actually the support squad.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How many platoons were there in the 2nd detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It had three infantry platoons, a support platoon, and a rear platoon, so it was five all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were the commander of all five of these platoons?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were all five of these platoons located in Sekovici?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No. There was one from Skelani. That was the 3rd infantry platoon, and that was stationed in Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us how large was that platoon?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It numbered about 20 or 30 men, depending on how many were wounded or sick and how the manpower levels were made up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know who the commander of that platoon was?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. Milenko Trifunovic, also known as "Cop".

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Cop is his nickname?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, what kind of uniforms did the 2nd detachment wear?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Mostly a uniform consisting of two parts and overalls.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What was the colour of the uniform?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That would be green camouflage?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, it was kind of light brown, coffee coloured.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Was there an insignia?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. The special police brigade, those words were on our left arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But did it designate whether you were from -- that it was from Sekovici?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, everybody knew if the number was 2000, then that was the Sekovici platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So there was a way of distinguishing which units were from Sekovici?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about for the platoons? Was there anything on the insignia that would give some indication as to what platoon the police officer was from?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, because there were numbers. Every policeman had a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you indicated that you were the commander until June 15, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How do you remember that it was that day?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Because I had a meeting with the then minister of the interior Tomo Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: In early June, I received orders to move the unit to the Sarajevo region from commander Goran Saric, the commander of the special police brigade. At that time, I refused because on the 19th of May 1995, I had applied to be discharged of my duty as platoon -- detachment commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why had you applied to be discharged of your duties?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Because I disagreed with the commander Goran Saric about the distribution of equipment and materiel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so I take it from your previous answer you didn't want to move to Sarajevo to be near this individual that you disagreed with?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, after your meeting with Kovac, was any -- was there a resolution?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. It was agreed that Rade Cuturic who had been my deputy up to then should take over the detachment. He was nicknamed Oficir, and that I should go on annual leave. And after that, I would be transferred to the administration for anti-terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, this gentleman who went by Oficir, had he been the deputy before? Had he been your deputy?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: For about a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you're not there to command and say you are on leave, does he as deputy fill in as acting commander? Would deputy commanders --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. He had orders from the minister to command the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So it wasn't just merely his position, the fact that he was the deputy; he also had specific orders. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So on June 15th, after June 15th, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I was on annual leave. And as my wife was pregnant, I went with her to her family in Krusevac. The whole family was there together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Where is Krusevac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It's in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How far would you say from the Bratunac area?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think about 250 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How did you get there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: By car. To Krusevac, you mean? By car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And whose car was it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: The car belonged to a company in Sekovici which often lent us that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Does that company have a name?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. Transport.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's the name of the company, Transport Company?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, Transport Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it was their car and not a car from the detachment that you used to go to Serbia. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, how long were you there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I stayed there until the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, did your wife give birth by then so you could leave?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So why did you leave? I mean, if she was about to give birth, and that's kind of a momentous occasion, at least I'm told, why did you leave?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: On the 15th of July, I was to meet the minister, Tomo Kovac, in order to be issued with a document appointing me to my new position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where were you to meet him?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I was supposed to call him on the phone first, and then meet him either in Bijeljina at the ministry or in Pale where the ministry had a branch office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So on the 13th, you left Serbia. Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Cacak, Uzice, Ljubovija, Bratunac, Milici, Vlasenica, Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, why did you go to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: That was the route I had to go in order to arrive in Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before leaving to go to Bratunac, had you heard any news about Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. On television in the evening of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you went to Bratunac, did you stay -- did you stop?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I arrived in Bratunac around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: And...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you stop at Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, because I had a sister there, and I was planning to go and have lunch at my sister's.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. All right. So please tell us -- you told us that you arrived in Bratunac at noon. So what happened when you arrived there? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: In the very centre of Bratunac, I encountered Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where did you encounter him? You said in the centre. Was he walking? Was he driving? Was he just standing?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He was walking, and I saw him and stopped my car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Incidentally, do you know where the police station is located in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. He was just leaving the police station and going toward the centre, and I was just entering the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So what happened when you saw Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I stopped, got out of the car, and greeted him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So I take it you knew him?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. He had been my superior up to that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please describe to us what exactly the two of you talk about.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I asked him how he was, what was new, and he said that the Srebrenica operation was underway, that the 2nd Sekovici Detachment had arrived in Sarajevo the previous evening, that they were in the area, and that they had just set out that the detachment was securing the communication and that he was on his way to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. The 2nd detachment had arrived from Sarajevo. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes, from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And did he say that they were on their way to Zvornik or that he was on his way to Zvornik? Which of the two? I'm not clear.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He said that the detachment was securing the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje communication and that he had just set out to get them out of there and to send them off to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did he tell you -- did he tell you -- first, were you aware prior to meeting with Mr. Borovcanin that the detachment that you had been the commander of and that was now being commanded by Oficir was in Bratunac or in the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did Mr. Borovcanin tell you how he got to Bratunac? Who ordered him?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Mr. Borovcanin tell you whether he was under anyone's command, that he had been subordinated to anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he say whether -- did he say who gave him the orders, if anyone, to go now to where his men were and to send them on to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he tell you who had ordered him to send his men in the first place to go to secure the communication or the road over there where they were situated?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ask any of these questions?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is there a particular reason why you didn't ask, like, why are my men over there, what's going on?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I didn't feel the need at the time to ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Incidentally, how were you dressed at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, what kind of civilian clothes? Help us out here.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I had a track suit on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you wearing boots or tennis shoes or regular shoes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I was wearing a track suit and tennis shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you armed?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you have a bandanna on or maybe a helmet so at least you would look like you were in some sort of a military activity?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How long of a conversation -- how long did this conversation last with Mr. Borovcanin when you first encountered him in the centre of Bratunac as he was walking out of the police station?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Five, maybe ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did he -- where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I went to my sister's, to her home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And where does she live? You said Bratunac, but where exactly.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: In Lamele in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I understand you gave your sister's name to the Prosecutor when you were being questioned. Incidentally, is your sister still living in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Her name is Mirjana Vukic, and her man is called Milovan Lukic, and they still live in that flat, that apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you told this to the Prosecutor, if they wanted to go and check the story when you were there, how you were dressed, what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you go to see your sister. What happens? What do you do?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I arrived at my sister's. She got lunch ready. I had lunch with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Two or maybe three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And after that, I take it you left?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. I set out towards Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, before setting out, did you change clothes or were you in the same clothes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: The same clothes. I didn't change.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, for those of us who have never been to that area, in order to get to Sekovici from Bratunac, where would you normally have to travel through? What's the route?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Bratunac, Kravica, Konjevic Polje, Milici, Vlasenica, Tisca, my village, and then Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So tell us after you left your sister's home, or her apartment, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I set out towards Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you get there right away?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No. When I passed Kravica, I saw the members of the 2nd Sekovici Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So tell me, what happened when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I stopped my car and started chatting with them, asking them how they had fared in Sarajevo, how they were. I asked them if they were tired.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we've heard testimony that there was ongoing battle activity during that day. Did you notice any?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: There was sporadic gunfire all along the road. As soon as I got out of Bratunac, there was sporadic shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Weren't you concerned, given that you were dressed in this workout uniform and had no weapon? Weren't you concerned when you stopped there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, I was used to it by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you tell us, if you recall, with whom did you speak? Some of the names.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I talked to all of them. I remember I talked to Cop and Oficir and Rade Cuturic and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How long would you say you were with the men at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think I spent two or three hours with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And while you were there, before we talk about any particular event, while you were there, did you notice anybody from the 1st company, the PJP of the Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So please tell us what -- first of all, where exactly did you stop? You said you went past Kravica. I take it you know where the warehouse is, the agricultural warehouse. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, and I take it you're travelling in the direction of Konjevic Polje. Can you please tell us, how far did you travel before you saw the men of the 2nd detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: About a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And were they all bunched together or were they spread out?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, no, they were still securing the road. That means they were spread out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. While you were there, did you notice whether they were calling anybody, any of the Muslim men in the column that was going towards Tuzla? Do you know whether any of those men that you had been associated with were calling out for the Muslim men to come down and surrender themselves?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you notice any men surrendering themselves, coming out of the woods?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice it there. But I did see a group up there on the meadow, about -- well, between 50 and a hundred men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And how far away or how close were you to where the men were situated in the meadow?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: 50 or a hundred metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I understand the terrain, when you get to Sandici, it's sort of a little hill. Are you -- have you gone over the hill? Are you behind -- or are you just by the hill? Where exactly were you situated?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I was on the edge of the hill facing Kravica. And there was some water across from where I was, a spring of water.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we were to visit the area, we will see right as you get to the hill on the left side there is a house that has been pretty banged up. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Are you right at the house, before you get to the house, or past the house?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Before the house toward Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you haven't passed the house towards Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you make any inquiry as to who those men were and why they were there and who was securing them and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, we were talking about how it was up there by Sarajevo and we talked about whether they were tired, how much they had to do, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you notice whether any of these men were being abused in any way?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you notice whether these men were being guarded?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're not suggesting that they were not guarded.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: That's not what I'm saying, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What you're saying is that you didn't notice anybody guarding them. Is that what you're saying? Just so we're clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Leading is really too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It was for -- I'm told that there was a perhaps something lost in the translation. That's why I had to, but very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you know what happened to those men?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: While I was there, some unknown soldiers arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: And took the people away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, where did they arrive from? From which direction?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: They arrived from the direction of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that would have been from the direction of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you notice how they arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: They arrived on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us approximately how many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, I would say roughly 10 to 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: They were also wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But did you notice any particular insignia that would at least give you some indication where they were from?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you speak with any of them?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you were there, on which side of the road were you standing or sitting talking with your men? Was it the right side or the left side of the road?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: The left side of the road coming from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje. That would be the left side of the road, from that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on which side of the road is the meadow?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: On the right-hand side of the road, a little higher up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And on which side of the road were these men walking on, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And you said earlier you did not recognise any of them.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you overhear any conversation that would at least give you some sort of indication who might they be, who had sent them there, what their tasks were?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Incidentally, from where you're standing, is the road flat or is there an elevation? Or are you on top of the elevation? Which of the three?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, I was at a slight elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you notice what these men did eventually?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you see where they went?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: They went up towards Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But wait a second. I thought you told me they were coming from the Kravica direction. And I'm talking about the soldiers. I'm sorry if I confused you. Where do these soldiers go to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, the soldiers went towards the Muslims who had been taken prisoner who were on the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And did you notice what, if anything, they did with these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: They took them and lined them up in a column and took them off towards Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before this, had anyone come by, any higher echelon officers that you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. General Mladic with his escort passed by.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And how far -- did he stop or did he just keep going?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He stopped and said something to them, talked to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Were you able to, from your distance, were you able to hear what General Mladic was saying?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: From that distance, I wasn't able to understand what he was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, why didn't you get closer to hear him and perhaps even greet him?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Because I was wearing civilian clothing, and the general didn't like the police and the police in civilian clothing, he would probably have given me grief on account of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How long was the general there with the men, speaking to the Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: As long as it took to deliver that speech, to say what he had to say to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then in which direction did he leave or did he go towards?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He went off in the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, eventually what happened to the men that were sitting in that meadow?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Then the soldiers took them and lined them up into lines and took them away towards Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. When they were taking them away, did you by any chance have any conversation with the soldiers then, or did they make any remarks that you could hear?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know at the time where they were taking the men?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you notice whether these men had a komandir, commanding officer?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And did you keep an eye to see where these men would eventually would go?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, they went in the direction of Kravica, that way, by the road. They took the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, at that point in time do you know with whom you were speaking with, at that location where you were situated?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: With Trifunovic and Oficir and someone else. I don't know what his name was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Trifunovic you indicated goes by the nickname of Cop. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, he was the commander or the komandir of the -- the battalion from Skelani. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, no, he was the commandeer within the 3nd platoon within the 2nd detachment of Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that. And Oficir was -- had taken over your position as the komandir of the 2nd detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He was the commander of the 2nd detachment of Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So he was a commandant?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, we're about to get into the section where I would rather not break it up because it's going to take a little while to get through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we may have a break right now. We'll resume at 20 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Stupar, we left off at the point in time when you saw the men that was sitting in the meadow being taken away by some unknown soldiers heading in the direction of Kravica. Now, could you please tell us what happened sometime later.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Some 20 minutes later, a member of the platoon from Skelani came up. His name was Krle, or rather we called him Krle. That was his nickname. I think his name was Krsto whether his surname was Savic or not, I'm not quite sure, but I think Krsto was his first name. He asked the late Oficir, he said he had heard that there was a neighbour of his among the group, and he had to ask his neighbour something and wanted to find him for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And continue.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: And Oficir said that he wouldn't go alone, but that he would accompany him. And after that, the two of them went off, and I stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Before Oficir made that decision, did he turn to you to get permission from you, since you had been the commander, you were on leave at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, but I wasn't the commander at that time. He was in command of the unit, so he didn't need to ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So off they went. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I stayed behind, and I went on talking. There was the commander of the platoon from Skelani there, Cop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then what?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Some 20 minutes later or half an hour later, we heard intensive shooting coming from the direction in which Oficir and Krle had just left. 12

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was there any other shooting going on at the time that you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, there was sporadic shooting throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But from the location where you were situated, you are now indicating you were able to hear -- some intensive shooting was coming from the direction where Oficir and Krle had left. In what direction would that be?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: In the direction of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Incidentally, when they left, how did they leave? By what means?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: They went on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, once you heard this intensive shooting, what did you do, if anything?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I took up the radio station from Cop, and I contacted Oficir straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What kind of communications were you using again?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: We had a hand-held Motorola GP 300, a radio station of that type.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Whose was it? Whose Motorola was it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: The one I took belonged to the komandir or commanding officer of the 3rd platoon, Cop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How did you know to communicate with Oficir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: We had the call signs from earlier. He was Laser 62 or sometimes Oficir, depending on the time. But we knew each other's voices. We could recognise each other's voices so we didn't actually have to resort to the call signs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Just so I understand correctly, it was you who placed the call or he called you, which of the two?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think I placed the call. I called him and asked him what was happening, whether it was going on somewhere nearby him, where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What was the response?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He said that Krle was dead and that he had -- he was wounded and that he needed a vehicle to take him to hospital urgently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what did you do after hearing that information?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I had planned to go and see what had happened in my own car straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before getting into your car and going off in that direction, was there another call?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. Ljubisa Borovcanin called because he heard me but he didn't hear Oficir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Had you seen Mr. Borovcanin prior to this?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, I had seen him prior to his going off in the direction of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So the last time we talked about Mr. Borovcanin, you had seen him in Bratunac in the centre. So my question, just to be precise for the record, from the time of the incident that you heard about in Kravica and the time that you had seen him previous to that in Bratunac, where had you seen Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I saw him there, in the part where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, did he -- how is it that you saw him? Did he stop? Was he walking? Was he driving by? Was he being driven?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He was standing there. He was walking around before he left for Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know how he had gotten there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you notice whether -- did you notice his car or a car that might have been driving him?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think he drove a grey car. I don't remember what make.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was there with any military officers?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you speak with Mr. Borovcanin when you saw him there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Not even a "hello"?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, yes, we would say hello to each other, and then he continued to issue some orders to Oficir, which I didn't hear, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, when he was giving -- issuing these orders to Oficir, how close were you to Oficir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: 10 to 15 metres apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And after Mr. Borovcanin left, did you at any time ask Oficir "what did Borovcanin tell you, what orders did he issue"? Did you make any inquiries?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: When Oficir returned, came back to us, came up to me and Cop, he said that Borovcanin would let him know when he would move the unit to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you recall, if you could tell us, from the time that you saw Borovcanin to the time that you heard this intensive shooting, how much time had elapsed?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. In any event, getting back to our story, where we had left off before, it was after you had your conversation with Cop that you recall having a conversation -- I'm sorry, after you had your conversation with Oficir, you had your conversation -- you had a conversation with Mr. Borovcanin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How was he able to communicate with you if he had left?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, as soon as I had finished talking to Oficir, he called because he hadn't heard Oficir but he had heard me. So he was in some sort of -- well, Oficir's Motorola didn't have the range to reach him where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Just so we're clear, because some of us are not very familiar with this equipment, if you could just tell us a little bit because I don't want to be leading you, how Mr. Borovcanin could know that you had this conversation with Oficir or know that there was a problem? How is it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He probably heard my conversation, and then asked me whether everything was all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How could he hear your conversation? That's what I'm trying to get at. Help us out here.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He just heard me on the same channel. He was working on the same channel. The Motorola and him was on the channel, and he could hear me but he couldn't hear Oficir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If he had a Motorola and that Motorola was on and on the same channel, he would be able to listen in and hear the conversation, or at least part of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that would depend on the range and the terrain, of course?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please explain to us what exactly you told Mr. Borovcanin at that time.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I told him that something was wrong with Oficir. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then what? What did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I got into my car and drove off towards Oficir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How long did it take you to get there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, I drove as fast as I could, and the distance is about 1 to 1 and a half kilometres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And -- now before setting off, did you know exactly where to find -- where Oficir was located?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you're driving. How do you know where to stop?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, he said he would be waiting for me on the road, and I just drove.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And did you find him on the road?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He was standing on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us where exactly he was standing.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He was standing by a warehouse at the entrance to Kravica on the right-hand side. He was on the road by the warehouse. 10 to 15 metres away was the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, had you been to that warehouse before?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you saw him standing there, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I stopped, opened the door for him because you couldn't open the door from the outside --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you had to get out physically or did you just reach over?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, no, I just reached over and opened the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then what?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He got into the car and I drove off towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, he had told you over the Motorola that he had been injured. Were you able to see what injuries he had sustained, if any?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: His right hand was singed. I don't know whether it was the left or the right, but I couldn't see the extent of the injury and how serious it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you stopped the car to let Oficir in, could you please describe to us what, if anything, you saw and heard that was happening by the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I saw the soldiers who had taken those people off. They were standing around and you could hear sporadic fire. It wasn't intensive fire, but just sporadic fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you said it wasn't intensive fire, it was sporadic. Earlier you told us you heard some intensive firing?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you're making a distinction now from the first to the one that you heard?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you notice, could you see where you had stopped the car to let Oficir in, could you see what the soldiers were firing on?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you have any idea as to what they were firing on?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you see any bodies of men laying on the ground from where you were situated, from the road?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How far from where you parked your car or stopped your car to let Oficir in, how far is it to the entrance of the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: 20, 30 metres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, is it flat or is there some sort of elevation, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that you let Oficir in your car and then you drove off. In what condition other than you told us that he was holding one of his hands, you don't know which one, that it was singed. Other than that, in what condition was Oficir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He was very pale. His face was contorted, and he complained of great pain. He was moaning and complaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, from there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Once he got into the car, where did you go with him?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I didn't get out of the car at all. I simply continued on toward Bratunac and then went to the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, okay. Now, how long did it take you to get to the health centre?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know. I was driving as fast as I could, as fast as the situation allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How long would you say you had actually stopped to let Oficir in, into the car? If you could tell us in seconds or minutes.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Only for as long as it took for me to open the door and for him to get in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the way to the health centre, you've indicated that he's in pain and that he's moaning. Did you ask him what had happened?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what it was that you learned from Oficir as you were driving him as fast as you could to the health centre to get some medical attention for one of his hands that had been singed?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He told me that when they arrived there, Krle entered the warehouse. He went about a metre or two inside with weapons, and that then they caught him, that they grabbed his rifle from him, that they shot him with his own rifle. And when he went to help Krle, they pointed the rifle at him. He grabbed the barrel and moved the barrel away from himself. And they shot for as long as there were bullets in the round.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, what kind of a rifle are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It was a Kalashnikov, an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did he tell you approximately how many rounds were set off, if he told you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, he didn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And how would his hand get singed from just grabbing the barrel? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, he grabbed the top of the barrel with his hand while they were firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that would -- so, from the heat, the barrel would --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did he tell you after he was able to -- after the automatic rifle was out of bullets, out of rounds, what happened?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He then went outside. He ran outside, that is, and they ran after him, and that is when the shooting started.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he tell you how far he had gone into the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He was at the entrance, perhaps a metre in, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us who it was then after he was running out that began firing?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Those who were standing around, providing security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was Oficir able to tell you or did he tell you, I should say, whether any of his own police officers from the Sekovici detachment, 2nd detachment, whether they were there along with him and Krle when Krle went into the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Incidentally, when you stopped to pick up Oficir, did you notice any other members of the 2nd detachment there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the soldiers or anyone else there, anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Is there anything else that -- well, let me ask you this: After he told you all of this, did you ask any other questions of Oficir, like why were they shooting at all of these people? That's a question that would come to mind, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I didn't ask him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Oficir ever tell you how many men, Muslim men, were in the warehouse at the time this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, from there, you took him to the health centre. Where is that located, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: In Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know how to find it, or did you have to stop and ask for directions?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I knew where the health centre was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, incidentally, did you ask Oficir where was Krle, where was the body of Krle, what had happened to it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He said that it had stayed behind there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I take it -- let me ask you this: When you got to the health centre, did you stay there or did you just drop off Oficir and leave?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Oficir went into the surgery, and I waited for him outside in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
