utterances.text: Do you recall how long you waited?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. But while I was waiting for him like that, Ljubisa Borovcanin arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we go into -- let me ask this: Do you know whether -- do you know whatever happened to Krle's body? Did you ever see it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: On the 14th at the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And now we're talking about the 13th. Right? This is still the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some documents, what has been previously admitted as P464A and I think there's one B as well. Perhaps just a -- there is a B as well. If you could look at that, and if you see anywhere --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could perhaps take the English version and put it on the ELMO for the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you see the name of Oficir there anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Rade Cuturic, father's name Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That would be the second name from the top?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recognise what this is incidentally, this piece of paper that I've shown you? Would you know what it might be, at least from reading it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, this looks like some sort of protocol.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if we look at the -- at that particular name in the first column going from left to right, it says the hour of 1740. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think that's about the time when I brought Oficir to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- and then if we go all the way to the other side, to the right side, can you read what it says, the notation. Are you able to read it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I can only distinguish the word "burns."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, what about Krle, the individual that was nicknamed Krle, do you see his name there anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Krsto Dragicevic, so his last name was Dragicevic, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Does it say what time for him?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It says here 1900.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we go all the way, if we go towards the, again, the right, it says "deceased," does it not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that's the individual that we're talking about when we're saying Krle?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Incidentally, the first name, we see there's a Miroslav Stanojevic. Did you know this individual?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it says there under the first column, date of wounding, 13 July, 1730. So that would have been about 10 minutes before Oficir. Did you notice whether anyone else was wounded when you came by the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Incidentally, Kravica, there's nothing -- there's nothing on -- where it says "place of wounding," it says "Kravica." There's nothing here that designates whether it was Kravica the village, the area, or Kravica warehouse, agricultural warehouse, does it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it, as you stand here today, over the years you haven't heard of Mr. Stanojevic and perhaps how he got injured in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, when Mr. Borovcanin came to the health centre, what was the nature of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He asked me what had happened, and I told him what Oficir had told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was his reaction?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: While I was telling him, when I finished talking, Oficir came out from the surgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now you say surgery. Was he having surgery, or was it the OR, the operating room, the emergency room?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think they just cleaned and dressed his wound. While I was there and talking to Borovcanin, he had been inside the doctor's office for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And -- okay. Now, you were saying that you had this conversation with Borovcanin, and you told him what Oficir had told you. What was -- did Mr. Borovcanin say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: When Oficir came out, he explained to him how the incident had occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then what?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: After that, we talked about Krle, about his corpse and what had happened to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: And that somebody should go to Skelani to prepare the funeral and inform the family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And who was designated to do that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I was designated to go to Skelani to prepare the funeral and inform the family. And Borovcanin would go and see where his body was and what had happened to it because we still didn't know that, and have it got ready in Bratunac and transported to Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I have a couple of questions. First of all, when you had that conversation with Mr. Borovcanin over the Motorola which was immediately after Oficir had told you that Krle had been killed and that he was injured, did you explain to Mr. Borovcanin where this incident had occurred, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I didn't know where the incident had occurred, so how could I explain that to Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know then when you met Mr. Borovcanin at the health centre whether Mr. Borovcanin knew by the time he met you, that is, at the health centre, whether he knew that this incident had occurred at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know from your conversation with Mr. Borovcanin whether Mr. Borovcanin had stopped by the Kravica warehouse on his way to Bratunac as he was coming now from the opposite direction, he was turning around -- he was heading towards Zvornik, now he was turning around. Do you know whether he had stopped at the Kravica warehouse to find out what had happened before meeting you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't remember him saying anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But you do recall that part of the conversation was what had happened to Krle, where the corpse was?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. In that conversation, I told him what had happened. Then Oficir came out and joined in the conversation. And after that, we discussed what had happened to Krle's body and where it was. Then Borovcanin said that he would take care of that and that I was to go to Skelani to inform Krle's family and see about organising the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to also clarify another point. You're on leave. You were in Serbia with your wife who is about to give birth, coming back two days early -- earlier, having already made arrangements to speak with Mr. Kovac on July 15th when this incident occurs. So if you're on leave, why would Mr. Borovcanin give you an order to go to Skelani now to take care of these arrangements?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It wasn't an order. It was an agreement. It was the humane thing to do, to express my condolences to the family and help organise the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, was this some sort of a unique procedure or was this the normal way of doing things, that is, when someone got killed in the line of duty from your particular unit, that somebody from the unit would go to inform the family and hopefully that person would be an officer?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: That was the usual practice. When someone was killed in the line of duty, one went to see the family, express condolences, help organise the funeral, and do everything that was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, earlier, if I may recap your route to go to Sekovici, you would go from Bratunac through Kravica, through Konjevic Polje, then onwards past Milici, Vlasenica, and so forth. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: On what day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I mean, that would be the normal route.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, for those of us who haven't been to Skelani, how would you go from Bratunac? Would you take that same route, or would there be a different route that you need to take?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No. Skelani is in a completely different direction. I had to go through Serbian territory via Ljubovija and Bajna Basta to go to Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What did you do after you made this agreement with Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I got in my car and went to Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you tell us approximately how long it would have taken you to get from Bratunac to Skelani?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you tell us the distance.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think it's some 60 or 70 kilometres, maybe a hundred. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you tell us about when did you get to Skelani?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think it was just beginning to get dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do once you got there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: There was a house there in which the Skelani detachment was quartered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, just go on. Tell us.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I announced myself. There was a duty officer by the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I explained to him what had happened. And then I went with him to Krle's family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what happened -- where did you stay that night?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I stayed in Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What happened the next day?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: On the next day in the morning, the funeral was organised, and the funeral was that very afternoon. And I attended it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you know whether the body of the late Krle came, had arrived by then?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it arrived during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when -- how long did you stay in Skelani?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I stayed there until the late afternoon of the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where did you go from there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Bajna Basta, Ljubovija, Bratunac, and then home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, so you had to go back that route, you had to go back towards Bratunac, and then would you go Konjevic Polje, Milici, Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's that route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would that be on the 14th or is that on the 15th when you head back?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: 14th in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what was happening, what did you notice on the roads? What kind of traffic did you encounter?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: At that time, it was difficult to pass through. There were people, soldiers, police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where were they located?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly. They were all over the place. The units weren't deployed in any special way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you notice whether the 2nd detachment was located where you had left them the previous day in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, maybe -- I just want to make sure that I'm clear. Were they there, or you didn't notice them there? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: They weren't there. On the 13th during the night, Cop arrived with his platoon to attend the funeral. And he told me that the detachment gravitating towards Sekovici had gone to the base in Sekovici while the Skelani detachment had gone to their base in Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And when Cop arrived, you say he arrived in Skelani. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's where the platoon is from, in fact?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it the late Krle was from that platoon?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I didn't ask you this question, so I'm going to ask it now a little bit out of order. But getting back to the 13th, when you were there for that period of time, meeting and talking with your mates from the 2nd detachment, what kind of traffic did you notice on the roads?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: A lot of vehicles were passing by, buses, vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you notice who was in these vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: They were full, and I think it was mainly with women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you make any inquiries, who were these people, where they were going, what was going on?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I didn't ask around. I knew they were Muslims from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, what about military hardware? Did you see any particular military hardware on the road while you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't remember. I think I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you see any tanks, any Pragas, any other vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: When I arrived, there was a tank there, and later it left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know who was driving that tank?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know what unit it was from?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just one last question before we move back into where we left off, do you know Momir Nikolic, also goes by the nickname of"Penzijica," "little pensioner" or "little pension"?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: After the war, I had a coffee with him in Bratunac. But otherwise not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you by any chance notice him over there while you were -- from where you were situated?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, getting back to where we had left off, it's late -- the 14th of July, you've left Skelani, and you're going all the way to Sekovici. Could you please tell us about what time you arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It was already late into the night. I arrived home and went to bed straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you stop anywhere from the time that you left Skelani, did you stop at any particular location, Bratunac, to visit the sister that you had lunch with the day before or two days earlier or anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, moving to the next day, July 15, could you please tell us what you did that day.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I was at home sleeping. When I got up, I went to the command of the detachment in Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: And I was to hear Tomo Kovac, to talk to Tomo Kovac there. But when I arrived, they told me to report to the Zvornik centre where Ljubisa Borovcanin was waiting for me. And he phoned up from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Who told you, if you recall, who told you that Borovcanin was waiting for you at the Zvornik centre?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't remember who the duty officer was, but the duty signalsman told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if my recollection is correct, it's some distance between Sekovici and Zvornik. It's a bit of a drive.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, it's about 50 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. For me, it's a bit of a drive. Did you call up before you went over there to speak with Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The message that you were to go there, did it give you any indication of the nature of what was waiting for you once you got to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No. He just said, he just left a message that as soon as I arrived, if I arrived there, if I came there, and if I didn't come there, that they were to find me and tell me he was waiting for me at the Zvornik centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Incidentally, officially, at this particular period of time, because you told us that on June 15, you were taking your leave and your command had been taken over by Oficir. So officially, what was your position with the detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, officially means judging by the papers, so I was still commander of the detachment. But all the commanding and everything else was done by Oficir, whereas I was on leave. And I was to be deployed to another post and I was supposed to receive the papers. But as you know, the paperwork was always a little late in our parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But in your -- if I may go back to what you had told us a little earlier, as far as you recollect, Oficir had gotten specific written orders placing him as the commander during that period when you were absent, or might -- did I get that wrong?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, no. He received an oral order from the minister, Tomo Kovac, on the 15th of June at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we'll get back to this issue. But let's carry on with what's going on at this period of time. On the 15th of July, you get that message to go to the Zvornik centre. What do you do?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I took a driver and went off. I passed by my house, and I got dressed there, and I would pass by my house anyway. That's the way the route goes. And then we set off for Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How were you dressed?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know exactly whether I was still wearing my track suit or whether I put something else on. I really don't remember. But I do know that I put my overalls on at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you have a weapon with you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you go to Zvornik. And what happens when you get there? Where do you go?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: We took the road to Vlasenica, Milici, Zvornik. And we arrived at the centre in Zvornik. And in the office of the chief of the centre, Dragomir Vasic and Ljubisa Borovcanin was waiting for me, and the deputy of the centre, chief Mane Djuric was also there I believe. Perhaps there was somebody else, but I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you notice anything on the road during the drive from Sekovici to Zvornik, any traffic that caught your eye on that particular morning?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, just so we're clear, is there some sort of a relationship between your detachment, your position as the -- you know, in the -- your detachment I should say and Mr. Vasic, who is the head of the centre there in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No. We had two different chains of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you had nothing to do with Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got there, could you please tell us what was the nature of this meeting? What transpired?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't an official meeting of any kind. Ljubisa told me that I was in command of the unit again, that they had heard that -- or perhaps that he had seen the minister on the 14th and this was conveyed by the minister. And they discussed a situation that was rather specific for Zvornik; that is to say, there was a group of Muslims, well-armed Muslims there, and they had already broken one of the defence lines up at Kula Grad. And if they were turned towards Zvornik, the question was whether they would take control of Zvornik, so there was a lot of discussion about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did Mr. Borovcanin show you any documentation verifying his conversation with Mr. Kovac, putting -- placing you back as the commander of the 2nd detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No. He just said he had talked to him and that the man had said because of Oficir's wounding, that I would be in command of the detachment until the end of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after that, what did you do? After this little gathering where you had this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: After that, we went to the headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade, to Standard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall about what time it was?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It might have been about 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Had you been to Standard before?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So this was your first -- the first opportunity you had to go to the Zvornik Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall where in the Standard building or Standard building you went to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: When I entered the building, I went up the stairs, and I think to the right there was a large operations room or something like that. The door was to the right, or at least I think that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did you go alone or were there others with you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: There was me, there was Ljubisa Borovcanin. There was Dragomir Vasic, and I think Danilo Zoljic as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you all walking up the stairs together or did you come separately, or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. Leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour. I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did -- were the others with you when you went up the stairs?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. All four of us came together and went up the stairs together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you mentioned an operations room, and then you said that there was another room. Which of the two rooms did you go into?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I didn't say there was another room. I thought it was the operations room. So once we had gone up the stairs, it was the first door to the right. I think it was the operations room. Anyway, it was a large room we went into.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you went into that room. But if I understand you correctly, you're not certain whether that was, indeed, the operation room?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I wasn't sure, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Incidentally, did you know back then Mr. Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you saw him as you were walking up the stairs?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it you didn't check the building to see whether he was in the building at that particular time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you got to that room, could you please tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: When we went inside, in there was Obrenovic, Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, just Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Obrenovic at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, that was the first time I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you know of him, of his position, his rank?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I had heard about him previously, but I didn't know about his position or rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please describe to us what happened during that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, he said that there was a large armed group there. He said there were ten to fifteen thousand of them. 6.000 of them were well armed, over 6.000 well armed Muslims were in the region. And it was in the region from Zvornik to Baljkovica, but he didn't know exactly where within that radius, and they were discussing what should be done. They were afraid that they would turn toward Zvornik, and if they did so, they could take control of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what was the response to Mr. Obrenovic's remarks?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, mostly everybody shared that opinion. When I say "everybody," I mean Vasic and Borovcanin. They held the same opinion about the situation. And they tried to find a way out, a solution to the situation. And one of the solutions was that a line should be opened and let them through from Baljkovica to get to the Muslim territory, and the other solution was to make double lines in the area; that is to say, not to allow them to exit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And again, for clarification purposes, what was Mr. Obrenovic's estimation as to how many armed Muslim men he was facing?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: About 6.000, I think. That's what he said at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well armed. Now, when he was describing this, how did he appear?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, he appeared sort of disturbed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I didn't want to lead you. That's why I didn't feed you the potential answer. So what was the -- after that, after that exchange, what happened? What was finally determined?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: They were all in favour of opening the line and letting them come out because of their assessment of the forces, their forces, our forces, the ratio until Obrenovic talked to someone over the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: After that, he said that the commander, Pandurevic, would be arriving soon, that he was already somewhere thereabouts, and that he had an explanation for everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did Pandurevic ever show up?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, he came very quickly. And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat "and what."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me ask you the next question. Had you known Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, I had known him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you knew him personally, or you knew of him?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I knew him when there was some celebrations and ceremonies, things of that kind. He would always be there. That's how I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when he showed up, what exactly happened then?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: When Obrenovic presented the situation to him and he said that we were in favour of having the lines opened, that solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What did Mr. Pandurevic say to that? What was his reaction to that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, he reacted by saying that he had clear-cut orders, and anybody who didn't wish to listen to him could leave this area. That was his area of responsibility. And I say that double lines had to be set up and they were not to be allowed to leave. He said something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so then what was decided?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, we weren't asked any more. Pandurevic set out the plan on the map where each unit was to be positioned, and these double lines to be set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where was this -- where were the lines set up? Was that in the Zvornik town or was it in the terrain? Could you give us an indication.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: We were told to go to the region of Baljkovica, I think, that general area, and that we were to take up our positions at a slope there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Were you given particular coordinates on the map to position yourselves?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No. We were just told to report to the battalion command there. I don't know what the battalion's name was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Were you told by Mr. Pandurevic as to who was going to be giving you orders?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did Mr. Pandurevic ever give you specific orders at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, he said where the first company that was there with us, that they should take up positions where they said, in which part, and that we should report there they battalion headquarters, and that they would show us the exact location.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When Mr. Pandurevic was going on in noting where the various units would be situated, was Mr. Borovcanin there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And at that point in time, would it be fair to say that Mr. Borovcanin was your commander?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know what arrangements Mr. Borovcanin, if any, had made with Mr. Pandurevic at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Mr. Borovcanin tell you who, if anyone, had sent him to Zvornik to have this meeting with Vasic and Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Mr. Borovcanin ever say that he and his units, including yours, had been resubordinated to Pandurevic and that henceforward you would be taking your orders from Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, he didn't say that. But we received that from Pandurevic directly. So Pandurevic said "I'm the commander here. This is my area of responsibility. Anybody who wants to listen can listen and follow orders. If not, I'll inform the command." That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. In your case, which command would he have been informing if Mr. Borovcanin was there and he was your commander?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you protest with Mr. Borovcanin that, you know, here was Pandurevic --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you recall at that point in time where the 2nd detachment was located? Had they mustered and were they there waiting for instructions?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, he was informed that he should come to Sekovici -- from Sekovici. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, what happened after this, after this meeting? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: We went back to the centre, waited for the detachment to arrive and for the first company to muster.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The first company. Now, which one are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: The first company of the Zvornik centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's commanded by whom?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: The commanding officer of the 1st company was Raso Pantic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- and what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: After that, so the units were assembling there, had lunch, and this was already into the afternoon, the late afternoon hours, and then we moved off into the direction of Baljkovica, that general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you go with the 1st company? Did you go together there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was the 1st company subordinated to the 2nd detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But if I understand you correctly, there are two different lines of command.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now was there anyone there from the Zvornik Brigade that would be commanding, giving orders, instructions, maybe even coordinating the situation there so at least you knew who would be in charge?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: When we arrived in the area, Baljkovica, we went down into a valley and there was a house there where the battalion's headquarters was. 10

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then what?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: And we found Obrenovic there. And I think the detachment commander was also there, or rather the battalion commander. I can't remember his name. And there was Legenda, Jolvic, in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Legenda is the commander of the wolves, the Drina Wolves. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's leading as is -- as are most of these. These are questions or they're testimony of the lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who is Legenda, this well-known figure that we have heard about for the last eight months in this trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. What this Trial Chamber is heard is not relevant and should not be stated to the witness like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who is Legenda?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, he led the Drina Wolves, that detachment, within the composition of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was he a well-known figure?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, we knew each other from the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what does his nickname, Legenda, mean?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, what happened when you got there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: We got up there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat what he just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We didn't catch all of your answer. So if you could repeat it, and please speak slowly so we can get the translation.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: This is how it was: We went down to see where the unit was to assume its positions. And the unit stayed up at the top, on top of the hill. It didn't go down to the command and headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then what?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: While we were talking there, I sent the driver off, the radio Motorola was -- the battery was empty. I sent the driver off to have the batteries recharged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: And after some time had gone by, we heard some shooting up there where the detachment and the 1st company had remained. And the driver was supposed to come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he ever come back?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. He ran back shouting "I'm yours, I'm yours." And the Muslims were running after him and shooting and crying out "Allahu Akbar."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then what? What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: After that, so that was towards evening, a battle started. The fighting started. It lasted half an hour to an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Was that the only battle that occurred while you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So at no other point in time was there any firing, any fighting?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: As I said, no. That was when the fighting started until it got dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Were there any casualties?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Not at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. At what time were there casualties, then?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: This was still the 15th. On the 16th, early in the morning, just as dawn was breaking, the fighting resumed. And then we realised that we were surrounded in the battalion command. There were about 40 of us altogether. We were trying to defend ourselves, and the detachment and 1st company which had remained outside the encirclement were trying to unblock us. The fighting went on until about 3.00 or 4.00 p.m., and I think we had three or four men killed and about 15 wounded. I don't know about the other units that were helping us, how many losses they had, what their losses were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Had you seen such fighting prior to this occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Believe me, I have been on quite a few war theatres, but I've never seen anything like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you talked about your casualties. Do you know how many Muslim casualties there were, if there were any?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please describe to us the strength of these armed soldiers, Muslim soldiers, so we can get an idea of, you know, what kind of a fighting force their strength is at this point in time, on July 16, some four or five days after they have left Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: It was a large group, as can be seen from the fact that when we broke through on the 16th at 3.00 p.m., we came out up there and Pandurevic ordered that the line be opened for them to leave. As they were leaving, the whole valley was full of them. They took a jeep over, carrying it in their hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: There were so many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, had in your opinion, having been there, having lived through that experience, and based on your experience, had the line not been open when it was, could you give us an indication what in your opinion would have happened in light of the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think there would have been far more losses on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you think that eventually you would have been able to overcome that force or vice versa?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, after the lines were open, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: We stayed there for another two or three days securing those lines, making sure that they didn't come back from the federation or that they didn't infiltrate any sabotage units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now you say from the federation. Are we talking about there's another line as well separating the two sides?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No. We're talking about the territory controlled by the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you know which army, which division was situated there by any chance?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Whose?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Which division, which Muslim --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now during this incident or this period of time when you were situated there, what was Mr. Borovcanin doing?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't know. He wasn't there with me. I was in the encirclement down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What was the means of communication between you and, say, Obrenovic or the other members of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: We had communications with the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say centre, are we talking about the Zvornik centre which is the MUP centre that's Vasic's office?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Not Vasic's office. We reported to the centre, and then the centre put us through if we needed to talk to Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But which centre are we talking about? Is it the MUP centre?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: The Zvornik centre, yes. MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So while you're at the field, if you need to talk to Obrenovic, you have to call the MUP centre, and then pass a message on to them to contact Obrenovic, and then -- is that how it worked?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, no. What happened, for example, was that they also had their own lines. And if the battalion commander was there, we could talk through their line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, you would have to use their Motorola?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I just want to make sure, because I'm not clear on this, with your Motorola, assuming that they were not there, were you able to directly communicate with members of the Zvornik Brigade like Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, during this battle activity that you talked about, were you taking orders from Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Obrenovic was there with me, and he was asking for assistance from the military units using his own communications line. And I talked to my detachment, which had remained outside the encirclement and was trying to help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm trying to get a clear answer. I'm not sure I understand it. Are you both working side by side or is one over the other? Which of the two, to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: What was important to us was to get out of the encirclement. I couldn't explain it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, before leaving that meeting that you had where Pandurevic came in and gave his little speech about who is with me, fine, who else, I'll report them, did Pandurevic at that point in time instruct you or perhaps your commander, Commander Borovcanin that henceforward while in the field you, the commander of the 2nd detachment, would be taking orders from Mr. Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I don't know how much time we have left. I've kind of lost track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We still have an hour, more than an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I mean for the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We already passed that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that. We can take the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: May I ask you how long you will go in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just have some housekeeping matters, cleaning matters just to kind of tie up some loose ends here and there. So I would say no more than 10, 15 minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think it's high time for us to take a break, and we will resume at a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, your loose ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Stupar, you are aware, are you not, sir, that Mr. Borovcanin gave statements to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And are you aware that Mr. Borovcanin indicated to the Prosecutor at the time that he gave his statement or statements, I should say, back in February and March of 2002 that you been the commander of the 2nd detachment throughout that period, you know, from the time the 2nd detachment left from Sarajevo, which would have been around the 10th or 11th of July and onwards? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, now that you know that, is Mr. Borovcanin correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, he's not correct, and I don't know why he's telling this falsehood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin also indicated to the Prosecutor at the time that you had conveyed to Mr. Borovcanin that you had seen a gentleman by the name of Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Which Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe that he was referring to the gentleman who is from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever say that to Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know anybody who is rather famous or infamous from Visegrad that goes by Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Have you heard of anybody that goes by Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I have heard of someone like that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm trying to be precise with my questions. Okay. And which Lukic are we talking about? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think we're talking about or that you are asking me about this man who has been accused of war crimes. And he's from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. At that time, at that time, and we're talking about July 1995, did you know, personally, that is, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you see him? Did you see him at that time when you were in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just to make sure that we're clear, at that time, did you know what he looked like? In other words, you could place a face to a name so when you saw him, you could say, Ah, that's Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, by the way, what about Mr. Blagojevic? Did you know him at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Have you ever met Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't think so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did his name ever come up in your conversations with Mr. Borovcanin or Oficir or Cop or anyone else that you came in contact with when you were in Bratunac on July 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about thereafter, say, when you were in the Zvornik area, when you were engaged in those combat activities? Did Blagojevic -- the name Blagojevic, Colonel Blagojevic from the Bratunac Brigade ever come up on any occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we started by discussing the -- your statement to the Prosecutor. And I'm looking at this statement. And again, after you -- Mr. McCloskey had cautioned you initially, he cautioned you again. And he states, and I'm reading from the transcript, page 15, "what I need you" - and this is from line 20 - "what I need you to do before you get into the details is acknowledge the fundamental issue here is that you were in charge and commanding these troops, not overall command. We know that Borovcanin, Mr. Vasic, Mr. Tomas Duskojevic and the other commanders, and you are clearly one of those. In that, there is nothing criminal about that. We all know that the commander has certain responsibilities. That doesn't make you guilty in any sense. And others have been able to admit they were commanders. And so what I need you to be able to do is admit to me, that you, the truth about who was commanding the unit." Do you recall hearing those statements from Mr. McCloskey at the time you had begun giving the statement to them back on June 26th --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And at some point, you reiterated again, and perhaps again, that at no time were you the commander of the 2nd detachment on June -- on July 13th, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, as you stand here today, having taken this oath, being a police officer, an inspector nonetheless, knowing that that oath carries certain responsibilities and consequences, and knowing that you are still a suspect, are you still maintaining that during that period of time you were not the commander of the 2nd detachment when you were there seeing those troops on the 13th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, lastly, I want to show you a document that has come into this courtroom that has been identified as Exhibit P159. I will show you the Srpski version. Now, sir, have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, were you shown this document last night by me and my colleagues?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, last night your colleague showed it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And before we showed it to you, did the Prosecution when they met with you back on 26 June 2002, did they show you this document?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did they show you any documents that reflected what had been told to them by Mr. Borovcanin; that is, that you were in full command on July 13, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did they by any chance, if you recall, now that you have read the revised or cleaned-up version of your statement, do you recall whether they pointed out any specific areas in Mr. Borovcanin's statement of 20th February 2002 or 11 March 2002, read them to you, and perhaps give you the opportunity, having been confronted with statements by Borovcanin, to at least give -- your opportunity to give them explanations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This is all argument. There's no question there. He's arguing how evil the Prosecution is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am not arguing how evil --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, put your question in the simplest way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying, Your Honour. That's about as laconic as I can be at the moment, but I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did they ever show you concretely what Mr. Borovcanin had said and give you the opportunity to respond concretely?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could look at this back page, the last page, we have a signature there. You indicated to us that Mr. Borovcanin was your commander. Do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I didn't look at his signatures, but I think it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we have a -- over here under 20 July 1995, we have this -- that's the last set of paragraphs, three paragraphs. Correct? Do you see above the last three paragraphs, it says "20 July 1995..."?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just for clarification purposes, which of those three paragraphs to your understanding reflect the activities of 20 July 1995? All three? The first two? Or just the first?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Only the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So based on your reading of the original version and your understanding of the language and having read this document, could you please tell us - it won't be leading, Your Honour - if you can please tell us if the first paragraph reflects only as to July 20th, what do the other two paragraphs reflect?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: The first part does reflect what they did on the 20th of July 1995. The second paragraph is a continuation of the report from the field that preceded this paragraph, who commanded which units, that they had good cooperation, correct cooperation, who commanded which units. Then he states that the 2nd police detachment was led by Milos Stupar and Rade Cuturic, the 4th detachment was led by Mijo Dragicevic, the 5th by Palezica [phoen]. The forces of the special unit were commanded by Danilo Zoljic and sometimes Savo Sritinovic [phoen], the commander of the MUP special police unit. So the last two paragraphs refer to the entire terrain in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you. I just wanted to be fair to everyone and make sure that we understand, and correct me if I'm wrong, the last two paragraphs would appear to be sort of a conclusion of this entire document and not reflect the activities solely of 20 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So now that we've established that, so it's not taken out of context, I want you to look at that last paragraph because it's a little troubling here. It says here, and I think you read part of it, or perhaps all of it, "the 2nd special police detachment was led by Milos Stupar and Rade Cuturic" and it goes on.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Rade Cuturic is Oficir. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And frankly, we need to refer to him as "the late Oficir," don't we, because he has passed away, hasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So he is unable to come here to at least give us an explanation in the event the Defence wanted to bring him here.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us or give us an explanation, how is it that Borovcanin, Mr. Borovcanin, has indicated here on this piece of paper, which is P159 in the very last paragraph that you and - and - Oficir, Rade Cuturic, were leading the 2nd special police detachment? And I should note for the record that this is -- this report seems to reflect dates starting from, at least on the third page, it starts with 12 July, although it reflects that the unit came earlier.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Probably because Rade Cuturic commanded the detachment until the 14th, and I took over on the 15th, that's why he put us there because as you see, the 4th detachment, he just put down mirror drag Mijo Dragicevic, for the 5th, he put down only Palezica. And in the case of the 2nd detachment, he wrote down the names of the two of us. If I was detachment commander, why would he state the name of my deputy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what you pointed out was there were no designations of the deputies of these other individuals?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Stupar, I want to thank you very much for coming here. I have no further questions at this time. Mr. Stojanovic may have some questions, who represents Mr. Jokic. The Prosecutor may have some questions, as well as the Judges. I would appreciate it if you would be as frank and forthcoming with them as you have been with me. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. Good day, Mr. Stupar. We will try to go through a few characteristic questions that touch on our Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stupar, as I understood during the examination-in-chief, in the morning of the 15th, after you had received information in the command of the 2nd detachment that you were to report to the Zvornik security centre, you set out in the direction of Nova Kasaba, Konjevic Polje, and arrived in Zvornik. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that from Sekovici, there is another asphalt road leading to Zvornik which goes via Paprace, Zapardi, Crni Vrh, Orahovac, and reaches Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that this road would be a little bit shorter than the route you took to Sekovici?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that the reason you didn't take the road via Paprace, Zapardi, Crni Vrh, and Orahovac is the lack of security and safety on this communication because of the arrival of the column of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have information about this when you were setting out to Zvornik, that this communication was not safe for this reason?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes. The Sekovici police station warned everyone not to use that road because it was closed for traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And what did they say about the reason why was it was closed for traffic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think that a medical corps came by and that all its members had been killed and that since then that road was closed and was no longer used for traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We have the duty roster of the Zvornik Brigade where this fact is stated. I assume that you are familiar with this terrain. So would you say I was right in saying that the area of Srpska Snagovo was practically cut off from the headquarters in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now go back to the 15th. At around 11.00, you say you arrived together with Vasic, Borovcanin, and most probably Danilo Zoljic to the command of the Zvornik Brigade. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you found Obrenovic in the operations room you mentioned, which is upstairs?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall whether Obrenovic said anything to you at the time as to where and when he had come from that morning?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does your answer "no" mean that he didn't tell you or that you don't remember him saying anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I don't think he spoke about that. I don't actually remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you happen to notice whether there were any other soldiers or officers there from the Zvornik Brigade up there on the first floor and in the office you were in?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: The room we were in, there weren't any. I don't remember having come across anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point in time during the examination-in-chief, you said you knew Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how you came to know him, where you know him from, where does it date back to.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I know him because he worked on some roads in the Sekovici area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When was that? When did Dragan Jokic build roads in the Sekovici area?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: He worked there after the war, and I think prior to the war as well, that he would come into Sekovici, and I saw him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have close contacts with him, or was it a superficial acquaintance?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if he knew me. I knew him. I knew who he was and what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you're quite certain that on that morning of the 15th when you went with Vasic and Borovcanin and possibly Danilo Zoljic that you didn't see him there at the headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, I'm certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stupar, we had testimony here by Mr. Obrenovic, and he spoke about how he went in together with Mr. Vasic to the command of the Zvornik Brigade, and that he happened to meet Major Jokic on that occasion. Now, in view of what you have said here today and the way in which you described entering the headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade and where you came across Obrenovic, would I be right in saying that what he was actually saying does not reflect the actual situation on the morning of the 15th?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'll try and clarify one more point for Their Honours, for the Trial Chamber, and to get to know the general area in which all this was going on. During the examination-in-chief, you say on the afternoon of the 15th, you received an order, and you went to Baljkovica, the area around Baljkovica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you said you received your deployment to take up your positions on a slope?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: We were supposed to take up our positions there, but we never reached that position. I didn't introduce my unit there because I went to the battalion command to see where that location was. But I never actually took up that position on that slope.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we then say that it was the Motovska Kosa, that slope, and it was in the Paloc area?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I think that's right, but looking at the house where the command was located on the right-hand side, we came from the left -- to the left of the house, and that slope was supposed on the right, to the right of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "right-hand side," for us to be able to orientate ourselves, are you looking at the BH army positions?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No, my back was turned towards their positions. Looking at it that way, with my back turned towards the BH army positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And just one more question, please, that I'd like to clear up. At one point in time you said that there was such a strong -- that there were so many of them and they were so strong that they could pick up a jeep in their hands. Could you tell us what type of jeep that was, whose vehicle it was, and what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it belonged to the Zvornik Brigade or whoever. But I saw them carrying the jeep. I think it had been seized. And I just saw them taking it away. I don't know who it belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So at one point in time, that jeep was to all intents and purposes in the hands of the BH army. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And just one more question in this area, this acquaintance of yours if I can put it that way with Dragan Jokic, what was your impression of him? What kind of man was he? Did he ever in your presence show any signs of nationalistic -- extreme nationalistic feeling or national intolerance, ethnic intolerance, that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: In the Sekovici region, where he was building the roads, and I sat with him one day, and I would not be able to conclude that that's the kind of man he was from the talk I had with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Stupar, for being so frank and forthright. I have no more questions at this point, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stupar.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How long have you been a criminal investigator?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Since the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And before that, did you do any regular police work, criminal investigations?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So for the three or four years that you have been a criminal investigator, have you been involved in criminal investigations of murder cases, for example?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Have you been to many crime scenes, many violent crime scenes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I was present, but usually they are inspectors for murders that undertake that kind of investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And in Bosnia, is the police job pretty much a 24-hour job whether you're on duty or not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, so far that's what it has been like. Now the laws are changing, but no changes actually yet on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If you're off-duty and you see a robbery in front of you, do you have a duty to do something about it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So as a Bosnian policeman, if you saw people being assaulted or abused, would you have a duty to stop that or do something about it as best you could?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In your experience, do sometimes police officers, as human beings like the rest of us, do they sometimes abuse subjects, people they had arrested, physically?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Ever heard of such a case in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, I have heard tales about that kind of thing, but not based on my own experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you about this issue of command. Were you on annual leave and still the commander on annual leave? Or were you not the commander any more?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Let me point this out to you: According to the agreement when we talked to the minister of the day, Tomislav Kovac, the agreement reached was that I should leave that duty and that the detachment should straight away, immediately, the very next day, the 16th, that the detachment be taken over by the late Oficir, to take them to the Sarajevo area to be in command of it, that I should go on annual leave. And once I returned from annual leave, that I should pick up my papers appointing me to the administration for anti-terrorist investigation. So we had already decided what position I would be taking up and what my duties there would be. But on paper, I was still the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Would you have had the authority to act as a commander still even -- for example, if you had come in on your leave, like many people do here? Would you have been -- would you have carried with you the authority of command if you'd come in on annual leave and, you know, done some official work? Or had you been officially relieved of your authority?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean, what authorisation, what authority?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, as a commander of the unit, you had certain authority, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, I had the authority to command the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And when you're on annual leave, you retain that command authority even though you're on vacation or on annual leave, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, it was like this: An agreement had been reached with the minister, Tomislav Kovac, and that agreement was that I was no longer in command of that detachment but that the person in command was the late Oficir. And when I come back from annual leave, that I should go on annual leave, and when I come back from annual leave, that is to say on the 15th of July, that we should see each other and I should pick up my appointment papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So in June, you made an agreement that you were no longer in command. Is that what you just said?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I had asked for already back on the 19th of May of that same year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's what happened. In June, you were no longer a commander.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: That's right. On the ground, no, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you had no real authority to do anything?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure what you mean. To do what? You say "to do anything." To do what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Anything as a commander.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And after you made this agreement with the superior, did you come into the office again or the command place before 15 July when I think you told us you went in?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: The command place, you mean. You mean the command place for the detachment? No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In fact, you left soon after that agreement and went to Serbia. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, towards the end of June. The end of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you do any work as a commander when you -- after this agreement that you'd made, any paperwork, take home anything, do any work like that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR
utterances.text: Well, I never did any paperwork when I was the commander. We had administrative services to see to the paperwork.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
